assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a new observational window with a cubic-kilometre detector in the Antarctic ice is a landmark of instrument-driven astroparticle physics. The 2013 detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and the later association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, established neutrino astronomy and probes cosmic-ray accelerators. The result is clear, original and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the IceCube concept and Karle was a leading figure in the detector construction and the discovery analyses. The credited pair is a natural, compact configuration. A large collaboration did the work and other individuals (for example early AMANDA/DUMAND pioneers) are outside the supplied credit, so some allocation questions remain.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed in several independent analysis channels, and the Galactic-plane and source evidence has strengthened. KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD are still maturing, so fully independent confirmation of individual sources is limited. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Individual source identifications (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) are at moderate significance and the origin of most of the flux is still open.
Credit relative to earlier detector pioneers outside the supplied names is a judgment call.
I am relying on my own knowledge of the discovery timeline rather than independent verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Resolving the shadow of M87* and Sgr A* at event-horizon scale is a decisive technical and scientific achievement, achieved through global mm-VLBI with demanding calibration and imaging. It gives direct tests of strong-field gravity and black-hole accretion physics.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow-imaging concept and Doeleman built and led the EHT VLBI effort. Zensus is an important institutional and technical leader but I would keep the prize to the two with the clearest decisive roles. The collaboration of over 300 people complicates the allocation and I expect colleagues to debate it.
assessment.maturity: Two independent targets, multi-epoch data and polarization images give good confidence in the images. Interpretation of the spin and the jet-launching physics is still evolving, but the core measurement is stable and mature enough.
uncertainties: Image reconstruction depends on priors and algorithms, and some critics have questioned the details.
Collaboration size makes a three-person limit contentious.
Falcke versus Zensus versus other leaders as the third name is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with the magic-wavelength trapping idea, reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and opened a new regime of precision measurement, including tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a path towards redefining the second. This is a measurement-technology advance of high lasting value.
assessment.attribution: Katori invented the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove it to record accuracy and many-body clock physics. The two-person credit is clean. Others (for example Hall and Hänsch frequency combs, already honoured in 2005) are not part of this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Many laboratories have independently reproduced and surpassed the performance, and the redefinition of the second is under way. The field is well confirmed, and the recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier 2005 and 2012 prizes on laser spectroscopy and atom control could be argued by colleagues.
Ion-clock competitors (Wineland-linked groups) may be seen as a parallel route needing recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Precision measurement of the acoustic peaks and anisotropies of the CMB, notably through WMAP, fixed the age, composition and geometry of the universe and underpins the standard cosmological model. The importance and clarity are very high.
assessment.attribution: WMAP is credited to Bennett as principal investigator, Page as an instrument and experimental leader, and Spergel as the lead theorist and analyst. Puget (Planck/HFI) and Sunyaev (acoustic/SZ theory) are also strong, so a three-person limit leaves out major contributors and the configuration is contested. Earlier 2006 and 2019 prizes also cover related ground.
assessment.maturity: WMAP and Planck confirm each other with high precision, so maturity is excellent. The recognition is overdue rather than premature, although the Hubble tension leaves some open questions.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2006 CMB prize and the 2019 cosmology prize.
Choice among WMAP and Planck leaders and Sunyaev or Zeldovich-school theorists is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model and required extraordinary detector technology, trigger and calibration work. The result is clear and permanent. The theory was recognized in 2013, so this would honour the experimental side.
assessment.attribution: Four credited individuals for two experiments exceed the three-person limit. Jenni and Virdee are founding proposers of ATLAS and CMS, and Gianotti was ATLAS spokesperson at the discovery. Della Negra is also a founder of CMS. Any trio drops a decisive contributor and this is the principal difficulty, in addition to the thousands of collaborators.
assessment.maturity: ATLAS and CMS independently confirmed the discovery, and coupling measurements are mature. Recognition is long-standing and arguably overdue on the experimental side, with a potential complication that Nobel statutes favour individuals.
uncertainties: Selecting three of four credited founders is contentious and may be seen as unfair.
The Nobel 2013 prize already recognized the discovery, which colleagues may regard as sufficient.
Whether the prize should honour a collaboration-scale effort via individuals is a policy question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting spherical aberration of electron lenses removed a century-old limit and gave sub-angstrom resolution in atomic-scale imaging across materials physics. It is a very good example of an instrument advance that created a new capability, with large lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Rose provided the theory of the aberration corrector, Haider built the first working corrector in TEM and Urban led its application to materials. The three-person split is clean and natural, with Krivanek an obvious missing name in related histories, though he is outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Aberration-corrected microscopes are now standard worldwide and the method is fully mature. Recognition, long since due, is timely in the sense of lasting evidence, though a chemistry prize might also be considered a better home.
uncertainties: It may be viewed as more naturally a chemistry or materials prize.
Missing contributors beyond the supplied credit (e.g., Krivanek) could be raised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background in pulsar timing arrays opens a new gravitational-wave band and probes supermassive black-hole binaries. It is an exciting measurement that depends on decades of patient timing and calibration work.
assessment.attribution: Contributions span three major PTA collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA) and the credited names reflect that spread. Manchester and Kramer are long-time leaders on pulsar timing, McLaughlin a NANOGrav leader, and Siemens another NANOGrav leader. Choosing three drops a key name and also underrepresents the independent collaborations.
assessment.maturity: The 2023 releases show a consistent signal across collaborations, but the significance is about 3 to 4 sigma and the Hellings-Downs correlation is not yet a definitive detection. Recognition is probably premature, and the astrophysical origin is unsettled.
uncertainties: Statistical significance is below discovery level for some analyses.
The origin (supermassive black-hole binaries versus new physics) is not resolved.
Allocation among three PTA collaborations is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon microstrip and pixel detectors transformed vertex and tracking measurements, underpinning heavy-flavour physics, the Higgs discovery and many applications beyond particle physics. As a detector builder I value this very highly as a technology that opens observational windows, although it is a technology prize rather than a single discovery.
assessment.attribution: Kemmer pioneered planar silicon processing for detectors, Parker developed microstrips and Heijne led hybrid pixel readout. The credit is plausible, but other groups at CERN and elsewhere (for example Rancoita, Hall and the Medipix and ATLAS pixel teams) also contributed, so the allocation is not obviously clean.
assessment.maturity: The technology is ubiquitous and fully proven, and recognition is long overdue. Whether it fits the physics prize criteria for 'discovery or invention' with enough singularity is the question.
uncertainties: Attribution across many detector-development groups is diffuse.
Committee appetite for an instrumentation prize is uncertain.
I am relying on my memory of the historical credit, not verified sources.
